title: Winning-case necessary condition (the one all 7 no-wins missed): knowledge must be EMPIRICAL / non-derivable
summary: The missing necessary condition for a memory/RAG win, sharper than "hard task + knowledge in graph": recorded knowledge must be EMPIRICAL — discovered by RUNNING/TESTING, NOT derivable by reasoning from the spec. All v1–v7 used reasoning-derivable knowledge → agent reasons to the same answer regardless → context only adds deliberation. A win needs knowledge the agent CANNOT reason to in-budget, only knowable by having-done-it ("scar tissue": "lib X truncates inputs>N", "approach A deadlocks under concurrency C", "fixture uses UTC but API returns local"). HARNESS = two-task chain with a TRAP: Task A (discovery) empirically uncovers a non-obvious fact + records it; Task B (beneficiary), DIFFERENT task, FRESH session (no memory of A), spec LEADS toward a plausible-but-wrong approach, cheap correct solution depends on A's fact. A/B = cold-B (no graph) vs warm-B (graph + semantic retrieval). WIN = warm-B solves at materially lower hardness OR solves where cold-B fails, beyond noise, + corroboration (warm not just writing less code). PHASE 1 = falsification: hand-author A's note as fixture, cold-B vs warm-B; if precise+empirical+retrievable+non-derivable STILL doesn't win, premise is dead. PHASE 2 = product demo: run A end-to-end (records via self-learn loop) then B benefits — proves loop closes + amortizes. RIGGING GUARD: cold-B must reliably FAIL/flounder first; if it solves cheaply the task isn't knowledge-dependent → invalid, don't fake. Feeds the gate with first POSITIVE labels. Implemented as task 688a3742.../5.
